Scaffy — Wave 1: the command corpus + the show-off showcase

Status: BUILDING — decisions D10–D19 locked, 8 slices filed, builders flying (showcase dispatches LAST). This is the wave Paper, the wave's living story. Digest appends the survey digest + verify plan; Decide appends decisions + the slice plan; Review closes it as the debrief.

The wish

"We will call it .scaffy instead now — also i want to see the full commands etc — run an epic cycle to give me an amazing show off with the commands actually shown — we want some really useful commands which touch what we usually do when developing on Barkpark."

Ground truth at wave open

  • Charter exists and is fresh (.claude/workflows/bp-scaffy-charter.md, D1–D9, authored today). D1 already seals the rename: the brand is .scaffy, no .nextgen in any new artifact.
  • Masterplan paper /papers/scaffy-commands-as-content is published and renders premium — but still says .nextgen in places (D8 patch owed).
  • NOTHING else has landed: no scaffy/ directory, no scaffy tasks in the ledger, no epic parent task. This wave files the whole tree.
  • Reference grammar survives at /Volumes/SATECHI/github/nextgen-vscode/ng-test-example.nextgen (22.8KB) — the lineage document, bugs and all.

Direction (Strategize — tentative until Decide)

The finished experience: you open one paper, scaffy-command-showcase, and it reads like a product launch. Six to eight commands, each one a chore you have actually done by hand on Barkpark — add a PortableDoc block type across four runtimes, add a docs card without blowing the 7-card cap, add an Oban worker with its cron line, add a CLI verb, add a plugin slice, add a migration. For each: what it does in one paragraph, an annotated file tree (● created / ○ injected), and then the entire .scaffy file in a code block — full text, zero elision — followed by a terminal mock of the run, the idempotent re-run (all guards hold, zero writes), and for the symmetry pair, the remove that leaves the tree byte-clean. The repo gains scaffy/commands/*.scaffy + scaffy/README.md. The masterplan paper is patched clean of .nextgen. No engine yet — and that is the point of the quality bar:

  • Hand-traceability (D7) is the bar. A reviewer must be able to apply any command manually. Every anchor unambiguous, every payload exact, occurrence explicit where an anchor could match twice.
  • Every anchor verified with evidence (D5). Builders grep the live tree and record file:line + quoted context per anchor in their task's acceptance evidence. A command that references a nonexistent anchor is a failed criterion, full stop.
  • The corpus defines the v2 grammar by example (D3). Fenced multi-line targets, MARK on every mutating op, payload-derived guards, declared VARIABLEs with casing transforms, SNIPPET/USE for shared payloads, closing ASSERTs that invoke real gates.

Choices I lean toward: flagship add-block-type (mandatory, D4) + symmetry pair add-docs-card/remove-docs-card (mandatory); then add-oban-worker, add-cli-verb, add-plugin, add-migration as the strong four — with add-api-route-parity only if survey proves router.ex anchors safe (it is ordering-hostile; if risky, drop it rather than ship a command that could misfire by hand). The showcase paper is the wave's crown: same native-block ingest path as the masterplan (POST /v1/plugins/bulldocs/papers, admin token), same premium vocabulary — eyebrow, ingress, stats, diagrams, terminal blocks. Merge lane per D9: new files only, no Elixir gate wait.

What matters most right now: anchor truth. The whole wave stands or falls on whether the injection points named in D4 exist at the quoted locations today. Survey verifies every single one against the live tree before Decide fixes the command set.

Survey plan (14 scouts)

  1. nextgen-grammar — full read of ng-test-example.nextgen: keyword inventory, known bugs, exactly what D3 hardens. Why: the corpus must be recognizably the same voice with the bugs designed out.
  2. anchor-block-type — verify all four add-block-type anchors (pdrender.go DefaultRegistry, render.ex render_block/2, JS registry.ts, root.html.heex edit CSS) with file:line + quotes. Why: flagship anchors; D5 evidence.
  3. anchor-docs-card — routing table rows, doc-tier headers, docs-anchors-check.sh + budget gate, current card count vs the 7-cap. Why: the symmetry pair must satisfy the real gates it ASSERTs.
  4. anchor-oban — the Oban.Plugins.Cron block in config.exs, one existing worker + its test as the payload template. Why: exact payload for add-oban-worker.
  5. anchor-cli-verb — how cli_commands/0 (tickets.ex:311 pattern) reaches the bp manifest; is it truly a one-line injection? Why: the 'architecture already made this a one-liner' story needs proof.
  6. anchor-plugin — minimal viable plugin slice: behaviour callbacks, discover_and_register, what tickets/ actually contains vs what a minimum needs. Why: add-plugin is CREATE-heavy; scope its true file set.
  7. anchor-api-route — router.ex ordering hazards, plugin register_routes contexts, SDK+capabilities parity chain. Why: go/no-go on add-api-route-parity.
  8. anchor-migration-schema — migration naming/timestamp convention, register_schemas/1 shape for add-schema-type. Why: two candidate commands share this ground.
  9. chores-mined — mine recent git history/PRs for repeated multi-file 'add X' patterns; rank by frequency. Why: the wish says 'what we usually do' — evidence beats intuition for the final command set.
  10. showcase-ingest — the masterplan paper's exact block JSON shapes (terminal, code, stats, diagram, table) + the bulldocs ingest contract + publish-wall/tag state for 'scaffy'. Why: the showcase builder needs a copyable recipe.
  11. masterplan-audit — every .nextgen/nextgen mention in the published masterplan paper, block by block. Why: D8 patch list.
  12. gates-for-assert — which repo gates run cheap and local (go test paths, docs scripts, js checks) for ASSERT CMD lines. Why: assertions must invoke real gates, not invented ones.
  13. merge-lane — which CI gates fire on a new-files-only scaffy/** PR; PR↔task gate requirements. Why: D9 promise must hold or builders stall.
  14. prior-art-scaffold — existing generators/mix tasks/make targets/tooling that overlap Scaffy. Why: a command should wrap or replace prior art knowingly, never duplicate it blind.

Ledger links

No epic parent task exists yet — Decide creates it and the slice tasks, then stamps wave_paper: bp-scaffy-wave-2026-07-16 on all of them. This paper will name the task ids once filed.

Survey digest (Digest phase, 2026-07-16)

13 assignments returned, coverage-accounted. Everything below is file:line-evidenced by the surveyors; rumors were discarded.

Established

  • Grammar settled. Full DSL inventory of ng-test-example.nextgen (697 lines). Seven bug classes independently re-derived from the raw file and matched the masterplan's own 8-row P0–P3 table exactly: 6× guard/quote-mismatch re-insert (single-quoted guards vs double-quoted payloads, :571–:656), path/URL casing divergence → real 404 (camelCase paths vs kebab hrefs), one unfenced 25-line REPLACE target (:385–410), the once-used unspecified CONTAIN START AND END OF TARGET magic, a triplicated 14-line payload, a weak import guard, and zero MARK/SNIPPET/USE/ASSERT CMD anywhere. D3(a)–(g) maps 1:1 onto these; the sentence-shaped voice carries over, the guard/mark/reuse/casing layer is new.
  • Anchors verified exact (D5): render.ex:182 render_block/2 · config.exs:223–224 Oban cron, last real tuple :251 (PlaygroundReaper) followed by a decorative comment block L252–256 — insert after :251, never after the comment · tickets.ex:311 cli_commands/0 · pdrender.go:241/:249 DefaultRegistry, 62 registrations.
  • add-cli-verb's headline claim is TRUE. A CLI verb is a pure data map appended in cli_commands/0 — no handler ref, zero Go changes (cli.go:7–10 documents zero hardcoding; dispatch is tree.Lookup → generic HTTP). One optional cosmetic polish exists: table.go:96 envelope-key hint.
  • add-plugin: charter D4 is wrong on "+ migration". No plugin ships a migration — schemas upsert via Bootstrap.register_all_schemas/0. And there are ZERO injection anchors (discovery is a disk-walk; the :plugins config is a kill-switch only): add-plugin is all-● CREATE (4 files). It also collides with live prior art: mix barkpark.plugin.new already generates exactly this shape from EEx templates — the command must knowingly supersede/wrap it, or be dropped.
  • add-docs-card: the 7-card cap is FULL today (check-doc-budgets.sh:78–84 hard-fails on ≠7; all 7 cards born in one commit, none ever added/removed). A real add can never land — the showcase demo must be a scratch create-then-remove that never persists an 8th card. Three touch points: CLAUDE.md routing row (gated), the card file with G1 header/anchors/2400B cap (gated), and docs/INDEX.md's Cards: brace-expansion line — which is invisible to the INDEX gate (regex charset excludes {},) — the one un-gated artifact remove-docs-card must sweep by explicit literal ASSERT, honestly labeled local-only.
  • add-api-route-parity: both reports converge on CUT. Real surface is 6 anchors, not 3 (router.ex + capabilities.ex core_cmd + 4 JS files: new module, index.ts barrel, client.ts method, types.ts); the manifest↔router "path-sanity cross-check" is dead code (_routes discarded, capabilities.ex:192); contract tests don't auto-extend to a new route. Catch-all hazards are real but localized to /studio and /w/…/p/… scopes — yet the JS-side anchor count alone fails the wave's hand-traceability bar. Charter's own fallback ("drop it") is the recommendation.
  • Showcase ingest recipe complete. Verbatim JSON shapes extracted for all 8 block types from the live masterplan (54 blocks). POST /v1/plugins/bulldocs/papers: requires {slug, blocks}, style defaults article, slug-keyed wholesale upsert; wall = description ≥20 chars + 1–12 tags {tag, strength 1–100 distinct, rationale ≥20}; auth = ingest token OR admin api_token. The scaffy tag is registered and published live. scaffy-command-showcase is a 404 — greenfield.
  • Masterplan D8 patch = 8 discrete edits: heading scf-018, code-lang tags on scf-020/022/025/032 (invisible in rendered view — a display-text grep misses 4 of 7), ascii tree scf-044, list item scf-053, plus the top-level description field (outside blocks[]). The related field (arrayOf reference→paper) is empty — the schema-native slot for the showcase link.
  • Gate truth, proven by RUNNING: safe ASSERT CMDs today = go vet ./internal/pdrender/... (0.5s) · CC=/usr/bin/clang go build ./... (6.7s; bare go build FAILS — cc is aliased to the Claude wrapper) · go test -run <Named> -count=1 (1.1s) · scripts/check-doc-budgets.sh (0.17s, green) · js tsc --noEmit/eslint/vitest run (all ≤3s, 185/185). UNSAFE today: the whole pdrender suite (4m24s and RED — TestNoInlineDivideFormulaOutsideSolver's unscoped grep sweeps sibling worktrees) · scripts/docs-anchors-check.sh (hangs >2min locally in check 5 — unbounded find hits .omx/worktrees) · mix format --check-formatted (red on main for an unrelated test file) · full mix test (never attempted; ~58MB free RAM, known OOM).
  • Merge lane (D9) holds, with corrections: main has ZERO branch protection and zero rulesets (live gh api 404/[]) — nothing mechanically blocks any PR. elixir.yml fires on every PR (no paths filter) but is convention-wait only and a scaffy-only PR needn't wait. doc-gates.yml triggers on ANY **/*.md repo-wide: the README/charter PR eats the full ~15-job suite (should pass — scaffy paths sit outside every check's scope); pure *.scaffy PRs dodge it entirely. pr-task-gate needs a Task: <id> body line pointing at an in_progress, claimed task.

Contradictions resolved / corrections owed

  • bp search "doesn't exist" (5 surveyors) vs works (3 surveyors): RESOLVED — the verb form is bp search query "<terms>"; bare bp search <terms> errors. Reproduced at digest.
  • Charter corrections owed at Decide: D4 add-plugin "+ migration" (false); add-api-route surface is 6 anchors not 3; D9 "dodges the Elixir Test lane" (it runs on every PR — it just isn't blocking and needn't be waited for).
  • router.ex "no grep-visible routes" (chores-mined) vs quoted route lines (anchor-api-route): resolved — routes are parenthesized macro calls get("/path", …); the failed grep assumed the unparenthesized form.

Checked and NOT found (absences that decide things)

  • No prior art for add-block-type, add-docs-card/remove, add-oban-worker, add-cli-verb — genuinely new ground. add-migration's only prior art is Ecto's own generator, unreferenced in any Barkpark doc.
  • No scaffy/ directory, no showcase paper, no epic task — all greenfield.
  • No single CSS injection anchor found in root.html.heex (6417 lines) for a new block type — the flagship's 4th leg is the wave's weakest anchor. UNPROVEN.
  • Elixir render.ex internal injection points (what a new type needs beyond the :182 dispatch) not mapped.
  • JS registry's true block count unreconciled (comment says 42; a quick grep sampled 18).
  • The ingest write path was never exercised (all read-side proof); payload-size ceiling unchecked (showcase ≈100+ blocks); callout tone enum beyond "info" unknown.
  • nextgen-vscode's parser source unread — CONTAIN START AND END OF TARGET semantics remain inferred (acceptable: D3 designs it out).

Verify plan (fleet in flight NOW — last look before Decide)

  1. flagship-4surface-probe (Opus, worktree, RUN-proof) — wire a dummy block type across Go pdrender + JS registry in a throwaway worktree and pass the real gates (CC=clang go build/vet/targeted test; js tsc+vitest); map the exact Elixir render.ex injection points and settle the root.html.heex CSS anchor: find THE anchor or recommend scoping the CSS leg out. Reconcile the 42-vs-18 JS block count.
  2. docs-gates-clean-run (Sonnet, fresh worktree, RUN-proof) — time scripts/docs-anchors-check.sh + check-doc-budgets.sh in a clean tree; pull doc-gates.yml CI durations; verdict on anchors-check as an honest ASSERT CMD and whether a one-line .omx exclusion is a wave prerequisite.
  3. ingest-write-proof (Sonnet, RUN-proof, live guerrilla) — prove write auth + publish wall with a deliberately wall-violating POST (expect 422 label_spine), then a compliant scratch paper on slug scaffy-wave1-ingest-smoke (expect ok:true + liveview_path), re-POST to prove wholesale upsert; read the Plug.Parsers body ceiling; enumerate callout tones; settle bulldocs.patch ops vs full re-POST for the D8 edit.
  4. exemplar-payloads (Sonnet, read) — census all Oban worker/test pairs (mirrored-simplest vs Prune); pick add-migration's template (alter vs create-table, read both in full); read all 4 plugin_new EEx templates verbatim; quote ticket.inbox's full map — the corpus quotes real files, chosen once, here.
  5. grammar-dry-run (Opus, read+grep-proof) — compose the complete add-oban-worker .scaffy under hardened D3 in-report, then hand-trace it per D7: grep-prove every anchor unique/pinned in the live file, prove guards are verbatim substrings of what the op writes, ASSERTs only from the proven-safe gate list. Any rule that doesn't compose = a D3 amendment now, not 7× rework later.

Decide — verify round results (2026-07-16)

Four verifiers, all with run-proofs. Trusting proofs over prose, the direction survives with three corrections.

  • flagship-4surface-probe — PROVEN with 2 corrections. A dummy wavecheck block was wired end-to-end. Go: registry map at pdrender.go:249–361, open (43rd type left the FULL suite green: ok github.com/FRIKKern/barkpark/internal/pdrender 0.934s). JS: registry is 42 types (not 18) and FAIL-CLOSED at 4 edits — emitter+map alone drove exactly one red: expect(registered).toHaveLength(42) … Tests 1 failed | 187 passed; a CASES fixture entry + count bump are mandatory. CORRECTION 1: the Elixir anchor is a compose_block clause before the catch-all at compose.ex:1190 — render.ex:182 is render_block/2, the entry, needs ZERO edits. CORRECTION 2: the CSS 4th surface is CUT — root.html.heex has no per-type anchor (9/42 ad-hoc editor rules only); block CSS lives in paper-surface.css; wavecheck rendered fine with zero CSS. Also: the charter did not exist in that worktree (now committed to main, 65cc4b7dc).
  • docs-gates-clean-run — PROVEN with a caveat. Fresh worktree: docs-anchors-check.sh exit 0 in 24s, PASS (12 warnings, 0 FAIL); check-doc-budgets.sh 0.104s PASS; CI corroborates (5/5 runs 26–31s). Primary checkout: stuck >115s at == canonical-for uniqueness == with zero progress (660 .claude worktrees). Verdict: legit ASSERT CMD with the clean-checkout caveat written into the command text. The .omx/.tmp-bp89 exclusion gap is real but filed as backlog (scaffy-backlog-anchors-omx-exclusion), not built this wave.
  • ingest-write-proof — PROVEN end to end, live on guerrilla. Wall fires (422 label_spine, nothing stored); compliant payload 200 ok:true, rev:"1"; same-slug re-POST = wholesale upsert (rev 1→2, no dup); /ops patch-block also works (key is id, NOT block_id — first attempt 422'd). Masterplan has exactly 8 .nextgen touch-points (blocks idx 17,19,21,24,31,43,52 + description) matching D8; already wall-compliant so full re-POST just works — CHOSEN over ops-patch. Callout tones: only success/warning/danger/info/neutral render distinct. Body ceiling 100MB. Residue: scratch paper scaffy-wave1-ingest-smoke (rev 3) — Review deletes it (backlog task filed).
  • exemplar-payloads — LOCKED with corrections. add-oban-worker: Prune is the cron exemplar but its test does NOT mirror its path; the Smoke pair proves the lib/test mirror convention. Crontab anchor reconfirmed: last real tuple PlaygroundReaper at config.exs:251, no trailing comma, decorative comment L252–258 after. add-migration: create_oban_jobs.exs is degenerate — exemplar is 20260714150200_add_chat_execution_event_projection.exs (10 lines, alter+partial index). add-plugin: all 4 plugin_new EEx templates quoted; THREE prior-art generators exist (plugin.new live, gen.plugin deprecated, gen_types different domain). add-cli-verb: ticket.inbox map spans cli.ex:87–104, not 86–105.
  • grammar-dry-run — the grammar COMPOSES; 5 amendments forced. A complete add-oban-worker.scaffy was composed and hand-traced: anchor unique (grep -cF full tuple = 1; bare cron string ×4, bare module ×2), guard a verbatim payload substring (=1 in payload, =0 in live file), 7-space indent preserved. Amendments A1–A5 (all accepted as D12): snake_case spelling; ASSERT CMD gate tiers (no Elixir gate is locally proven — TIER ci); comma-list append = fenced REPLACE of the last element; REPLACE guards mandatory/load-bearing; ASCII + brace-adjacency guard hygiene.

The composed add-oban-worker.scaffy (normative base for task scaffy-w1-add-oban-worker)

COMMAND "Add Oban Cron Worker" DESCRIPTION "Scaffold an Oban cron worker (worker module + test) and register its crontab tuple in the static Oban.Plugins.Cron block in config/config.exs — idempotently, on the shared :default queue." LAST_UPDATED "16-07-2026-00-00-00" DOMAIN "barkpark" TAGS "oban", "worker", "cron" CONCEPT "oban-worker" VARIANT "cron" VARIABLES
  VARIABLE 1 "WorkerName" TITLE "Name your worker" DESCRIPTION "PascalCase module suffix under Barkpark.Workers. Drives module name, file path (snake_case), test, and crontab entry." EXAMPLES "StaleTokenSweeper", "OrphanMediaReaper", "UsageRollup"
  VARIABLE 2 "CronExpr" TITLE "Cron schedule" DESCRIPTION "Standard 5-field crontab expression — how often the worker ticks. Opaque literal, no casing transform." EXAMPLES "0 4 * * *", "*/15 * * * *", "@daily"

# Worker module: Barkpark.Workers.{{.WorkerName}}
# module->file mapping is snake_case (lib/barkpark/workers/tag_distribution.ex
# == Barkpark.Workers.TagDistribution). Modeled on Barkpark.Audit.ExportWorker.
CREATE FILE IF ABSENT "api/lib/barkpark/workers/{{.worker_name}}.ex"
WITH
::: {{.worker-name}} worker :::
defmodule Barkpark.Workers.{{.WorkerName}} do
  @moduledoc """
  Oban cron worker — {{.WorkerName}}.

  Scheduled from the static crontab in `config/config.exs`
  (`Oban.Plugins.Cron`). Runs on the shared `:default` queue with
  `max_attempts: 1`: a recurring tick that runs again next cycle, so a single
  failed run should not retry-storm the queue.

  Fill in `perform/1` with the work this worker owns.
  """
  use Oban.Worker, queue: :default, max_attempts: 1

  require Logger

  @impl Oban.Worker
  def perform(%Oban.Job{args: _args}) do
    Logger.info("[{{.worker-name}}] tick")
    :ok
  end
end
::: {{.worker-name}} worker :::

# Worker test — proves perform/1 returns :ok; runnable as the scoped ASSERT CMD below.
CREATE FILE IF ABSENT "api/test/barkpark/workers/{{.worker_name}}_test.exs"
WITH
::: {{.worker-name}} test :::
defmodule Barkpark.Workers.{{.WorkerName}}Test do
  use Barkpark.DataCase, async: false

  alias Barkpark.Workers.{{.WorkerName}}

  test "perform/1 returns :ok" do
    assert :ok = {{.WorkerName}}.perform(%Oban.Job{args: %{}})
  end
end
::: {{.worker-name}} test :::

# Register the crontab tuple. PlaygroundReaper is the LAST static cron element and
# carries NO trailing comma; a bare INSERT below it yields two adjacent list terms
# with no separator (Elixir syntax error). So this is a REPLACE that re-emits the
# anchor line WITH the comma, then the mark comment, then the new tuple. Anchor is
# the FULL tuple (unique: count 1) — bare "* * * * *" occurs 4x, bare module 2x.
IN "api/config/config.exs"
### Append {{.WorkerName}} to the static crontab after the PlaygroundReaper entry
REPLACE
::: playground-reaper anchor :::
       {"* * * * *", Barkpark.Tenancy.Workers.PlaygroundReaper}
::: playground-reaper anchor :::
WITH
::: {{.worker-name}} cron :::
       {"* * * * *", Barkpark.Tenancy.Workers.PlaygroundReaper},
       # scaffy:add-oban-worker {{.WorkerName}} MARK:oban-cron-{{.worker-name}}
       {"{{.CronExpr}}", Barkpark.Workers.{{.WorkerName}}}
::: {{.worker-name}} cron :::
MARK "oban-cron-{{.worker-name}}"
ASLONG FILE DONT CONTAIN "# scaffy:add-oban-worker {{.WorkerName}} MARK:oban-cron-{{.worker-name}}"

# Post-conditions
ASSERT FILE "api/lib/barkpark/workers/{{.worker_name}}.ex" CONTAINS "defmodule Barkpark.Workers.{{.WorkerName}} do"
ASSERT FILE "api/test/barkpark/workers/{{.worker_name}}_test.exs" CONTAINS "assert :ok = {{.WorkerName}}.perform"
ASSERT FILE "api/config/config.exs" CONTAINS "MARK:oban-cron-{{.worker-name}}"
ASSERT CMD "cd api && mix test test/barkpark/workers/{{.worker_name}}_test.exs"

DEBRIEF — Review, 2026-07-16 (wave closed, grade A-)

All 8 slices came back green. Review fixed in place on -r branches; the lead merges the -r branches, not the originals. Every slice gate re-ran green on its final branch; the corpus was re-anchored against post-advance origin/main (two react-package merges landed mid-wave — all anchors held: core.ts:46/:727, toHaveLength(42), pdrender.go:249, compose.ex:1180/:1190, config.exs:251, cli.ex:88).

Grammar unification (the cross-slice pass)

The corpus DEFINES the v2 grammar by example (D3) — Review found three dialects and unified to one: IN "file" / INSERT AFTER FIRST|LAST <fenced anchor> WITH <fenced payload> / matching fence labels / kebab mark names planted BY the payload / ASLONG FILE [DONT] CONTAIN / quoted ASSERT CMD "…" [TIER ci]. Final op census (W2 fixture inventory): 11 CREATE, 5 INSERT AFTER FIRST, 1 INSERT AFTER LAST, 5 REPLACE, 1 REMOVE, 1 DELETE FILE IF PRESENT, 12 MARKs on 12 IN-ops, 30 ASSERT FILE, 14 ASSERT CMD (6 TIER ci), 1001 lines of .scaffy.

Ledger audit

Honest across the board: all 8 slice tasks in_progress with only merge-gated criteria open (the lead closes those on merge: criterion 5 on the flagship, 4 on oban/cli-verb/migration/plugin/docs-pair/showcase, 3 on readme; plus "exists on main" criterion 0 on docs-pair and showcase which ride the merge). Both builder deviations (showcase dispatch-last deadlock, docs-pair criterion-0 wording) were stamped as they happened. Review closed scaffy-backlog-smoke-paper-cleanup (smoke paper deleted, not_found quoted). No ledger lies found; no foreign tasks touched.

Open questions handed to W2 (ratify or reject in the validator)

  • A declared MARK with no plantable text — the docs-pair INDEX brace-line sweep (no comment syntax survives a brace expansion; the payload literal is the handle).
  • New-by-example spellings: REMOVE with consumed mark, DELETE FILE IF PRESENT, ASSERT FILE … EXISTS|ABSENT, positive-polarity ASLONG FILE CONTAIN on remove-direction ops.
  • CountBefore/CountAfter as a declared pair (grammar has no arithmetic) — validator lints the +1.

Grade: A-

What earns it: the corpus is complete, honest, and hand-traceable at a bar rarely hit — every anchor grep-proven, the flagship live-applied and reverted, the docs pair traced through a full add→red→remove→byte-clean cycle, the showcase live with its reproducibility mitigation proven under fire. What holds it from A: the corpus shipped speaking three grammar dialects — for an epic whose W1 deliverable IS the grammar-by-example, that inconsistency (plus one genuinely broken mark contract in add-cli-verb) is the exact defect class the wave existed to prevent; Review caught it, but the builders' cross-slice coordination did not.

Wave complete. Next: W2 parser + validator (bp scaffy validate/fmt), fixtures = this corpus as merged.
